title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
description: Discover the functional student hubs and quiet retreats across The Forest that define daily life at Drew University beyond the standard admissions route.

cards.title: Silent Study in the Kean Room
cards.subtitle: Rose Memorial Library, Level C
cards.notes: Visit Level C for a strictly enforced silent zone. It is ideal for deep focus sessions when the main library commons becomes too social for heavy academic work.
cards.short_summary: A designated silent study zone located on Level C of the Rose Memorial Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The Kean Room on Level C is designated as a silent zone for individual study.
cards.source_title: Find Your Zone | Silent, Quiet, Social and Hybrid
cards.access_notes: Open during regular library hours; accessible to students with a valid Drew ID.

cards.title: Relax at the 1867 Lounge
cards.subtitle: Ehinger Center
cards.notes: Head to the EC to find this lounge filled with comfortable chairs. It is a central spot to relax between classes or meet up with friends near the dining area.
cards.short_summary: A central student lounge located within the Ehinger Center featuring comfortable seating.
cards.evidence_claim: The 1867 Lounge is located in the Ehinger Center where students can relax and work in comfy chairs.
cards.access_notes: Located inside the Ehinger Center; typically open during building operating hours.

cards.title: Nature Retreat at Zuck Arboretum
cards.subtitle: Drew Forest Preserve
cards.notes: Walk the self-guided trails around the glacial ponds. It serves as a quiet woodland retreat for passive recreation and observing local wildlife like turtles and herons.
cards.short_summary: A 45-acre forest preserve on campus featuring glacial ponds and nature trails.
cards.evidence_claim: The Zuck Arboretum is open for passive recreation and serves as a woodland retreat with a self-guiding nature trail around its ponds.
cards.source_title: Biodiversity and Ecological Restoration at Drew
cards.access_notes: Trails are open to the public; visitors must close gates to protect the ecosystem from deer.

cards.title: The Commuter Hub
cards.subtitle: Ehinger Center
cards.notes: Utilize the recently renovated space featuring a full-sized refrigerator, microwave, and foosball table. It is the primary social anchor for non-resident students.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated lounge for commuter students in the Ehinger Center with kitchen amenities and social games.
cards.evidence_claim: The Commuter Lounge in the Ehinger Center features a large refrigerator, microwave, coffee machine, and foosball table.
cards.access_notes: Primarily for commuter students; located within the Ehinger Center.

cards.title: Laps at the Simon Forum Pool
cards.subtitle: Simon Forum & Athletic Center
cards.notes: Access the eight-lane, 25-yard NCAA pool for open swim hours. Remember to bring your Drew ID for entry at the Baldwin Gym Patio entrance.
cards.short_summary: An indoor NCAA-regulation swimming pool available for use by the Drew community.
cards.evidence_claim: The Simon Forum houses an eight-lane 25-yard NCAA pool open for the Drew community.
cards.access_notes: Valid Drew ID required for entry; check seasonal hours for open swim times.

cards.title: Historic Steps of Mead Hall
cards.subtitle: Mead Hall Entrance
cards.notes: Sit on the thick stone steps of the Greek Revival mansion. It is the historic heart of campus and a quiet spot for outdoor reading under the massive Ionic columns.
cards.short_summary: The grand entrance portico of the historic 1836 Mead Hall mansion.
cards.evidence_claim: Mead Hall features a full-height portico with six massive Ionic columns and ten thick stone steps.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor piazza is publicly accessible; interior houses administrative offices.

cards.title: Performances at The Space
cards.subtitle: Ehinger Center
cards.notes: Check the schedule for student-led coffee house events. This informal venue hosts comedians, poets, and musicians in a relaxed, creative environment.
cards.short_summary: An informal performance venue in the Ehinger Center for student creative expression.
cards.evidence_claim: The Space is a campus venue where comedians, poets, and musicians often perform in a coffee house style.
cards.access_notes: Open during scheduled events and building hours.

cards.title: Global Hub at Tilghman House
cards.subtitle: Tilghman House
cards.notes: Visit this center for cultural programming and international student support. It provides a dedicated lobby and meeting space for the global student community.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated center for international student services and cultural exchange.
cards.evidence_claim: Tilghman International Center provides a place for students and hosts educational and cultural programs.
cards.access_notes: Open to all students; primary hub for international student advising.

cards.title: Practical Needs at Pepin
cards.subtitle: Pepin Services Building
cards.notes: Go here to replace a lost ID card or borrow a shovel during snowstorms. It houses the Service Response Center and Public Safety desk for essential campus help.
cards.short_summary: The administrative hub for campus facilities, ID services, and public safety.
cards.evidence_claim: The Service Response Center in the Pepin Services Center handles ID card replacements and loans shovels to students.
cards.access_notes: Service Response Center open Mon-Fri 7:00 AM - 5:00 PM; Public Safety open 24/7.

cards.title: Casual Reading on the Couches
cards.subtitle: Rose Memorial Library, Level E
cards.notes: Climb the main stairs and turn left to find these comfortable couches. They offer a great vantage point for people-watching while catching up on light reading.
cards.short_summary: A casual study area with comfortable seating on the upper level of the library.
cards.evidence_claim: The second-story library couches are a popular spot for reading and observing the library entrance.
cards.source_title: Top 10 Best Study Spots at Drew
